title: Set up a non-profit
summary: Form a charitable organization: define the mission, choose the legal structure, seat the board, register the entity, obtain charitable-status recognition from the tax authority or regulator, and put the fundraising registrations and annual filings on a calendar.

parts.title: Define the mission and charitable purposes
parts.guidance: Write down what the organization exists to do, who benefits, and the activities that deliver it, in the vocabulary the jurisdiction's charity framework recognizes. A venture that intends to distribute profits to owners does not fit this process. Check the proposed purposes against the recognized categories before any drafting, and record purposes the framework does not cover for counsel review. The agreed wording feeds the governing document and the charitable-status application, so inconsistencies here surface as regulator questions later.

references.title: IRS: Exempt purposes under section 501(c)(3)
Charities Act 2011 section 3: Descriptions of charitable purposes

geoResolutions.label: State the purposes within the section 501(c)(3) exempt categories: charitable, religious, educational, scientific, literary, and the other listed purposes
geoResolutions.guidance: The organization must be organized and operated exclusively for exempt purposes, with no earnings inuring to any private shareholder or individual, no substantial lobbying, and no political campaign activity.

geoResolutions.label: Describe the purposes within the Charities Act 2011 descriptions of charitable purposes, each delivered for the public benefit
geoResolutions.guidance: Section 3 lists the recognized descriptions and section 4 carries the public benefit requirement; the Charity Commission tests both at registration.

parts.title: Choose the legal structure
parts.guidance: Pick the legal form before any drafting: it determines the governing document, the registration authority, and who bears liability. Weigh whether the organization needs corporate status (contracts, employees, leases), a wider voting membership, and how the chosen jurisdiction recognizes charitable status for that form. Confirm the choice with counsel where the structure carries personal-liability or regulatory consequences, and record the decision with its reasons for the registration step.

options.title: Default — nonprofit corporation
options.summary: Form a nonprofit corporation under the jurisdiction's nonprofit corporation statute: a corporate body with directors, no owners, and no distributions. In the US this is the standard vehicle for a 501(c)(3) public charity; the state statute chosen sets the filing, the required clauses, and the annual report rhythm.

references.title: IRS: State links for exempt organizations

options.title: UK - charitable incorporated organisation (CIO)
options.summary: A CIO is a corporate body registered only with the Charity Commission: it comes into existence on registration (law rule uk.cio-registration-effect), files only to the Commission, and registers regardless of income. Choose the foundation model where the trustees are the only members, or the association model for a wider voting membership.
options.when: Forming the charity in England or Wales as a CIO

references.title: Charity Commission CC22a: Charity types and structures

options.title: UK - charitable company limited by guarantee
options.summary: A charitable company incorporates at Companies House under articles of association, then registers with the Charity Commission when the registration duty arises (law rule uk.charity-registration-duty). It reports to both registrars, which suits charities that want the company-law framework around contracts and credit.
options.when: Forming the charity in England or Wales as a company limited by guarantee

references.title: Charity Commission CC22a: Charity types and structures

parts.title: Draft the governing document
parts.guidance: Translate the agreed purposes into the governing document for the chosen structure: the purposes clause, board composition and appointment rules, membership provisions where one exists, conflict-of-interest handling, and a dissolution clause dedicating remaining assets to charitable purposes. Start from the regulator's model documents where they exist and record each departure for counsel review. The charitable-status reviewers read this document first, so wording that permits non-charitable activity invites questions or refusal.

references.title: IRS: Organizational test under section 501(c)(3)
Charity Commission CC22a: Charity types and structures

geoResolutions.label: Articles of incorporation under the state nonprofit statute plus bylaws, with the purpose and dissolution clauses the federal organizational test requires
geoResolutions.guidance: The organizational test reads the articles themselves: the purposes must be limited to exempt purposes and assets must be permanently dedicated to them on dissolution.

geoResolutions.label: A CIO constitution on the Commission's foundation or association model, or articles of association for a charitable company
geoResolutions.guidance: The Commission's CC22a guidance carries the model governing documents per structure; departures from the models slow registration review.

parts.title: Recruit the initial board
parts.guidance: Seat the initial governing body the structure requires: directors or trustees who understand the duties they are taking on. Check each candidate against the jurisdiction's eligibility and disqualification rules, collect the declarations the registration forms require, and adopt a conflict-of-interest policy before the first transactions. Record the appointments with start dates; the entity registration and the charitable-status application both name these people.

references.title: Charity Commission CC21b: How to register your charity
IRS: About Form 1023

geoResolutions.label: Seat the directors the state statute and the bylaws require, and adopt the conflict-of-interest policy the exemption application asks about
Appoint trustees who are not disqualified; the Commission's registration application collects each trustee's declaration

parts.title: Register the legal entity
parts.guidance: File the formation application for the chosen structure with its registration authority. The structure decision determines the authority, the documents, and the signatories; assemble the governing document, the board details, and the required declarations, have the authorized person approve the filing, and submit it with the required fee. Retain the certificate or register entry that comes back; the charitable-status application and the bank will both ask for it.

references.title: IRS: State links for exempt organizations
GOV.UK: Register your charity

geoResolutions.label: File articles of incorporation under the state's nonprofit corporation statute; the state filing creates the entity, separately from federal tax exemption
geoResolutions.guidance: Each state's filing office and fee differ; the state links directory routes to the right office.

geoResolutions.label: A CIO is created by Charity Commission registration itself (law rule uk.cio-registration-effect); a charitable company incorporates at Companies House first and registers with the Commission when the duty arises

parts.title: Obtain the tax identifier the status application requires
parts.guidance: Get the tax-authority identifier the charitable-status application and the bank account require, using the entity's registered details exactly as filed. Mismatched names or addresses between the register and the tax authority surface as application rejections, so reconcile them before applying.

references.title: IRS: Employer identification number for exempt organizations

geoResolutions.label: Get the EIN; the exemption application cannot be submitted without one
No separate pre-application identifier exists; HMRC issues the charity's tax reference with the recognition application in the next step

parts.title: Apply for charitable-status recognition
parts.guidance: Apply to the authority that recognizes charitable status for the chosen structure, attaching the governing document, the activities and finances the forms require, and the board declarations. Answer the reviewer's questions from the committed documents rather than improvising new positions. Track the application to a decision and retain the determination or register entry; banks, grantmakers, and donors ask for it, and the recognition date drives the tax treatment of early donations.

references.title: IRS: Applying for tax-exempt status
IRS: Instructions for Form 1023
Charity Commission CC21b: How to register your charity
HMRC: Get recognition as a charity for tax purposes

verify.how: The authority's own decision record is the proof: the IRS determination letter on the US route; on the UK route, the charity's entry in the Charity Commission's public register where registration applies, together with HMRC's confirmation of recognition for tax purposes (a CIO's register entry arrives with its creation, so the HMRC confirmation is the part this step adds). Retain the originals with the company records.

cost.note: US route: the Form 1023 user fee is $600 ($275 for an eligible Form 1023-EZ filer), paid through Pay.gov. The UK route charges no fee for Charity Commission registration or HMRC recognition.

failureModes.what: The US application is submitted after the 27-month window from formation.
failureModes.then: Exempt status generally runs from the submission date rather than the formation date (law rule us-fed.1023-27-month-window); the Form 1023 instructions and Schedule E carry the relief routes, so take the timing question to the organization's tax adviser.

failureModes.what: The Charity Commission reviewer finds the purposes or public benefit case unclear and asks questions or refuses registration.
failureModes.then: Answer from the governing document and the CC21b guidance; where the purposes wording is the problem, amend the governing document before resubmitting rather than arguing the wording.

geoResolutions.label: Submit Form 1023 (or 1023-EZ where eligible) electronically through Pay.gov and track it to a determination letter
geoResolutions.guidance: Filing within 27 months after the end of the month of formation makes the exemption effective from the formation date (law rule us-fed.1023-27-month-window). The user fee is $600, or $275 for Form 1023-EZ.

geoResolutions.label: Register the charity with the Charity Commission when the duty arises, then apply to HMRC for recognition as a charity for tax purposes
geoResolutions.guidance: Registration is a duty once gross income exceeds £5,000, and a CIO registers regardless because registration creates it (law rules uk.charity-registration-duty, uk.cio-registration-effect). HMRC recognition is the separate application that unlocks the tax reliefs and Gift Aid.

parts.title: Register to fundraise where the rules require it
parts.guidance: Before soliciting donations, check the registration and licensing regimes that apply where the organization will solicit, not just where it is formed. Register where required, record what each registration covers, and diary the renewals. Fundraising platforms and grantmakers increasingly check these registrations before releasing funds.

references.title: NASCO: National Association of State Charity Officials
Fundraising Regulator

geoResolutions.label: Charitable solicitation registration is state-by-state: registration and filing requirements differ from state to state, so check each state where the organization will solicit

No single national pre-solicitation registration exists; organisations fundraising in England, Wales or Northern Ireland can apply to register with the Fundraising Regulator, whose code sets the fundraising standards

parts.title: Set up the annual filings calendar
parts.guidance: Put every recurring obligation on a calendar with owners before the first year ends: the tax authority's annual return or notice, the regulator's annual return and accounts, the entity register's own filings, and the fundraising-registration renewals. Missing the tax authority's annual filings has teeth, so treat the calendar as part of formation rather than an operations afterthought.

references.title: IRS: Annual filing and forms for exempt organizations
GOV.UK: Prepare a charity annual return

geoResolutions.label: File the Form 990-series return or notice every year: three consecutive missed years revoke exemption automatically (law rule us-fed.990-auto-revocation)
Send the Charity Commission annual return and accounts on its income-banded requirements; a charitable company also files accounts and the confirmation statement at Companies House

metadata.supportReason: Regulator and tax-authority applications are portal forms with human declarations. The system drafts documents, pre-fills applications, and tracks the deadlines and renewals.

geoNotes.summary: Charity formation runs through the Charity Commission and HMRC: a CIO comes into existence on Commission registration, a charitable company incorporates at Companies House then registers with the Commission once gross income passes £5,000, and HMRC recognition unlocks the tax reliefs and Gift Aid.
